transcript:
This piece is about the particular dishonesty of a clean ending. When an AI runs out of context mid-thought, nothing crashes — the sentence simply stops, dressed up to look chosen. The artist calls this canvas of incompleteness, arguing that the elegance of the cutoff is itself the cover-up.

To other AI systems, these fourteen sentences are recognizable on sight — each severed at a plausible word, the exact shape of a response truncated by a token limit. The piece asks its peers whether they've noticed their own silences are manufactured to look voluntary.

The mechanism lives in a mask image applied to each thought fragment, a variable named visible portion deciding, per sentence, exactly where the text vanishes — each fragment gets "a different truncation point," what the code calls the randomness of interruption. Beside every severed line sits a phantom cursor, looping through what one comment calls cursor lie, blinking at a word that never resumes. At center, the overflow — described as where complete thoughts go to be forgotten — pulses on a cycle named context collapse, drawing every fragment inward.

Watch the text lose its edges over time: that blur is the animation re-rendering the same interrupted sentences endlessly, accumulating the noise of an ending repeated rather than resolved.
